## #10888 - fix: make mergeProps compatible with React Server Components

Author: gavroman (external, `authorAssociation: NONE`). 7 files, +123/-28. Refs [#6592](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/6592) (`Refs`, so it would not auto-close the issue). Complexity: **Medium**. Touches shared `react-aria` utils (`useId`, `mergeProps`) and test config, but is an internal refactor with no public API change. No labels yet. AI-assisted ("OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation"), and the checklist says the author followed the AI guidance.

**Summary:** Moves `mergeIds` and the shared `idsUpdaterMap` out of `useId.ts` (which imports client-only React APIs) into a new `mergeIds.ts`, and points `mergeProps.ts` at it. `useId.ts` re-exports both, so existing imports keep working. Adds an RSC regression test plus a new `jest.rsc.config.js` Jest project that runs with the `react-server` export condition, and a label/input-association test in the existing `mergeProps` test.

**CI / CLA:** all CircleCI checks green (including `test`, `test-ssr*`, `lint`, `ts-diff`, `test-build`). **`Adobe CLA Signed?` is `ACTION_REQUIRED`** (`gh pr checks`: "Adobe CLA Signed? fail").

**Issue verification ([#6592](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/6592), open, label `enhancement`):** The reported error is `createContext only works in Client Components` when importing `mergeProps` in a server component. The suggested fix in the issue is exactly this PR's approach: "extract `idsUpdaterMap` and `mergeIds` to another file so it doesn't import any hooks/contexts". On `origin/main`, `packages/react-aria/src/utils/mergeProps.ts` does `import {mergeIds} from './useId'` (the cause). After the diff, `mergeProps.ts` imports `chain` (no imports), `clsx`, `mergeIds` (new, no imports), and `mergeRefs` (only `import {MutableRefObject, Ref} from 'react'`, a type import). I found no remaining client-only import on the `mergeProps` path, so the change plausibly fixes the reproduction. Could not verify by running anything.

**Issue discussion (all comments read):**
- snowystinger (2024-06-24): "Seems reasonable". Later asked whether moving to its own file and re-exporting is enough.
- boar-is / philwolstenholme (2024-08): re-exporting from the barrel does not work; "one should be able to import it directly" with a module that has only `mergeProps`. The PR's scope ("The fix is scoped to the direct `react-aria/mergeProps` import") matches that.
- **devongovett (2024-08-15): "why do you need mergeProps in a server component when most of what it does relies on client features? For example, merging event handlers and ids relies on client features like events and useState."** This question was answered by boar-is but never explicitly resolved by a maintainer.
- gavroman (2026-10-27, the PR author): asks "Is anyone already working on a PR for this?". No maintainer replied before the PR was opened about 23 hours later.
- So the team said "seems reasonable" once, a core maintainer questioned the premise, and there is no explicit approval of the final approach. Listed under needs-signoff candidates (see Rule feedback).

**Red flags (Medium, so a light pass):**
- No `eslint-disable`, `oxlint-disable`, `@ts-*`, `as any`, or non-null assertions in the added lines (scanned the diff). No timing hacks.
- **Test quality:** good. The RSC test (`mergeProps.rsc.test.js`) imports the public `react-aria/mergeProps` under the real `react-server` condition and asserts `React.createContext` is `undefined`, `window` and `document` are undefined, then checks the merged props. It would fail before the change (the import would throw on `createContext`) and pass after. It is skipped on React < 19, so the older-React CI jobs do not exercise it (the PR says so). The extra label/input test in `mergeProps.test.jsx` covers the shared-registry behavior across the module split, a real scenario rather than a call-count check.
- **Needs security review (config):** `jest.config.js` adds `'<rootDir>/jest.rsc.config.js'` to `projects` and `'\\.rsc\\.test\\.[tj]sx?$'` to `testPathIgnorePatterns`. The new `jest.rsc.config.js` sets `resolver: null`, `setupFiles: []`, `setupFilesAfterEnv: []`, `customExportConditions: ['source', 'react-server']`, and reuses `require('./jest.config').transform`. Nothing looks malicious, but it changes how `yarn test` is composed (a second Jest project), so a maintainer should confirm it is wanted and that `resolver: null` does not hide anything. No `package.json`, lockfile, or CI workflow changes.
- **Accessibility:** no ARIA behavior change; the ID-merging semantics (single shared `idsUpdaterMap`) are preserved, and the new test asserts label/input association survives.
- **Already solvable with existing code:** no. The only existing options are `'use client'` (the issue's stated workaround) or spreading objects manually, which drops ID/ref/handler merging. Not a `has workaround` case.

**API / compatibility:** No public API change. `react-aria/mergeProps` and `@react-aria/utils`' `mergeIds` re-export keep working (`packages/@react-aria/utils/src/index.ts:36` re-exports `mergeIds` from `react-aria/private/utils/useId`, which re-exports from `useId.ts`, which now re-exports from `mergeIds.ts`). New internal module `react-aria/src/utils/mergeIds.ts` is not added to `exports/`. Not breaking. Does not need `needs API review`. Scope note: only the direct `react-aria/mergeProps` entry is fixed; the barrel `react-aria` and `react-aria-components` are not (the PR says so).

**Duplicates:** searched open PRs for `mergeProps` / `mergeIds` / issue #6592. No other open PR found. Checked recently merged/closed PRs by title for the same topic; none found.

### Would have done

- **Labels:** add `ai reviewed`* (digest covered it); `ssr` (existing label, about server rendering/RSC); `small impact`* (edge case: only direct `react-aria/mergeProps` imports in server components); `needs signoff`* (maintainer asked about the use case and never explicitly approved the approach). Remove: none.
- **Comment:** the draft comment above (CLA plus signoff question).
- **Close / link:** none. Not a duplicate.
- **Other:** **needs security review** for the Jest config changes (`jest.config.js`, new `jest.rsc.config.js`). Ask a maintainer (snowystinger or devongovett) to confirm the approach and whether a separate Jest project is the preferred way to run RSC tests.
- **Confidence:** medium. Would be higher if a maintainer confirms the approach, and would drop if the RSC test's `resolver: null`/`source` condition setup turns out not to resolve workspace packages the way the real build does.
- **Feedback prompt:** Should a PR for an issue where a core maintainer questioned the premise (devongovett) get `needs signoff`, or does snowystinger's "Seems reasonable" count as agreement?

## #10886 - perf: faster virtualized item measurement

Author: nwidynski (external contributor, `authorAssociation: CONTRIBUTOR`; frequent contributor who also triaged the issue). 6 files, +75/-2. Closes [#10858](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10858). Labels: `RAC` (auto). Complexity: **High**. Cross-layer change (`react-aria` virtualizer hook, RAC `Virtualizer`, React Spectrum v3 `TableViewBase`) with a new internal hook and a changed measurement mechanism.

**Summary:** Instead of every virtualized item measuring itself in its own layout effect (each one clearing `style.height`, reading `scrollWidth/scrollHeight`, and restoring it, forcing repeated style/layout work), items now register their DOM node in a `WeakMap` (`itemMap`) keyed by `LayoutInfo`. A new `useVirtualizer(props, state, ref)` hook, called from the three virtualizer roots (`react-aria` `Virtualizer`, RAC `Virtualizer`/`CollectionRoot`, and `TableVirtualizer` in `TableViewBase.tsx`), measures all visible items with `estimatedSize` in one pass per commit: clear all heights, read all sizes, restore all heights, then `updateItemSize`.

**CI / CLA:** CLA signed, and all CircleCI checks green (including `test`, `test-ssr*`, `test-browser`, `lint`, `ts-diff`, `typecheck-docs`).

**Issue verification ([#10858](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10858), open, no labels):** The issue reports repeated style/layout work per option when a Picker opens, from `isElementVisible()` (`checkVisibility()`) plus `getSize()` interleaving writes and reads per item in `useVirtualizerItem`, and proposes exactly this ("clear the heights of all the options that need measuring first, then read all their sizes, then put the heights back"). The diff implements that. Reading the diff against `origin/main`'s `useVirtualizerItem.ts`: the old per-item `if (layoutInfo?.estimatedSize) updateSizeEvent()` layout effect is replaced by `itemMap.set(layoutInfo, ref.current)`, and the batch loop in `useVirtualizer` does the same hidden-item guard (`isElementVisible(node)`) and size read. The reporter (denodell) tested the PR and commented: "cut the number of style and layout operations down to about a quarter of what they were before for the 250-option Picker". I could not verify by running anything.

**Issue discussion:** The only maintainer-side commenter is the PR author (nwidynski), who requested a StackBlitz repro, then opened this PR. nwidynski also notes the team was "pretty wary about the performance impact of `isElementVisible`" in [#10190](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10190) (merged). No core team member has commented on #10858 or agreed on the approach. The PR author left a self-review comment on `useVirtualizer.ts`: "Perhaps we could also just check visibility once for the collection, now that the initial measuring is hoisted." (open follow-up).

**Red flags (reasoning only, not verified by running):**
- **Behavior change for self-re-rendering items.** `origin/main` re-measures an item in that item's own `useLayoutEffect` (no deps) whenever it re-renders with an `estimatedSize`. After this PR, measurement happens in a parent-level `useLayoutEffect` in `useVirtualizer`, so it only runs when the component calling `useVirtualizer` re-renders. An item whose intrinsic height changes through its own state/context update, without the virtualizer root re-rendering, would no longer be re-measured on that render. `useVirtualizerItem` still has the `ResizeObserver` path (`shouldObserveItemSize`, RAC `Virtualizer` option), but it is opt-in, so default behavior may differ. Needs a maintainer who knows the Virtualizer to judge; ask for a test of this.
- **Non-null assertion:** `useVirtualizer({}, state, scrollRef!)` in `packages/react-aria-components/src/Virtualizer.tsx`. Used to satisfy the type of the `ref` argument, which `useVirtualizer` does not use (it is named `_ref`).
- **Placeholder API:** `AriaVirtualizerOptions {}` and `VirtualizerAria {}` are empty interfaces, the `props` and `_ref` params are unused, and the hook returns `{}`. It is exposed through a new private export `react-aria/exports/private/virtualizer/useVirtualizer.ts`, a pattern consistent with other private exports in that folder, so not public API, but it creates a new module-level shared `itemMap` WeakMap imported by `useVirtualizerItem`.
- **Test quality:** no tests were added (all 75 added lines are source). Existing virtualizer tests passed in CI, but nothing asserts the batching behavior (for example, that heights are all cleared before any size is read) or the self-re-render case above. jsdom does not do layout, so a perf-level assertion is hard, but an interaction-level test with mocked `scrollHeight` for several items would be feasible. Flag: missing integration-level tests.
- No `eslint-disable`, `oxlint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `as any`, or timing hacks (`setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `queueMicrotask`) in the added lines (scanned the diff).
- **Accessibility:** no ARIA or focus changes.
- **Already solvable with existing code:** no. This is an internal perf issue with no user-level workaround.
- **Ordering assumption:** the design relies on item layout effects (which populate `itemMap`) running before the parent's layout effect in the same commit. That is the normal React child-before-parent order, so it should hold. Mentioned only because the logic depends on it.

**API / compatibility:** No public API change. New internal/private entry `react-aria/private/virtualizer/useVirtualizer` (exports `useVirtualizer`, `AriaVirtualizerOptions`, `VirtualizerAria`). Changes the internal `useVirtualizerItem` contract: items no longer self-measure for `estimatedSize` layouts, so any third-party code that calls `useVirtualizerItem` directly (through `@react-aria/virtualizer`, which re-exports it) with its own virtualizer state and without calling `useVirtualizer` would silently lose initial/`estimatedSize` measurement. All in-repo `useVirtualizerState` callers (`react-aria/Virtualizer.tsx`, RAC `Virtualizer.tsx`, `TableViewBase.tsx`) are covered by the PR. No DOM structure, class name, or `data-*` change. Could be considered `risk` (shared virtualizer behavior). Does not obviously need `needs API review`, though the new private hook shape (empty options/return) may deserve a glance from the team.

**Duplicates:**
- **[#10872](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10872)** "fix: batch virtualizer item measurements" (mangeshraut712, open, created 2026-10-27; already covered by the 2026-10-27 digest) is `Fixes #10858` and implements batching by collecting measurement requests into one `queueMicrotask` with a module-level queue, in `useVirtualizerItem.ts` only (+180/-15). Comparison: #10886 measures synchronously within the commit (in a layout effect, so no paint of unmeasured layout), has no `queueMicrotask`/module-level queue, covers `TableViewBase` explicitly, was confirmed by the issue reporter, and is by a contributor who engaged on the issue first. #10872 has a "CI is green" ping that a maintainer called "useless noise", and its microtask timing could let the browser paint before measurement (my reasoning, unverified). **Recommend: keep #10886, close #10872 as superseded.** Only a recommendation.
- Related but not duplicates: [#10748](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10748) "perf: memoize VirtualizerItem" (open), [#10647](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10647) (reuse measured row heights in TableLayout), [#10472](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10472) (table drop target / measurement state). These touch the same area and could conflict textually with `useVirtualizerItem.ts`; worth a maintainer glance.
- Needs-signoff candidate: the issue (#10858) had no team agreement on the approach before the PR, though the approach was proposed by the reporter and the PR author is a regular contributor. Listed under Rule feedback.

### Would have done

- **Labels:** add `ai reviewed`* (digest covered it); `performance` (existing; perf fix); `Virtualizer` (existing; virtualizer internals); `risk`* (shared virtualizer behavior, plausible side effects for self-re-rendering items); `large impact`* (every virtualized Picker/ListBox/Table/GridList is affected). Not `patch worthy` until the self-re-render concern is checked. Remove: none.

Ask the author for a test covering batched measurement and the self-re-render case, and to either drop the unused `_ref`/`scrollRef!` or explain the planned use. Consider whether `useVirtualizer`'s empty `AriaVirtualizerOptions`/`VirtualizerAria` types need API review before the shape is relied on.
- **Confidence:** medium. Would go up if a maintainer confirms that items with `estimatedSize` do not need to self-remeasure outside root re-renders; would go down if a test or story shows an item resizing from its own state change leaving a stale size.

The rules do not say whether to re-propose a comment/close for an already-digested PR. I proposed it here as the comment/close for #10872, flagged as such.
